# Education in Greece – Summary
Education in Greece is structured into distinct stages: preschool (ages 4–6, including compulsory pre-kindergarten and kindergarten), primary school (Dimotiko, ages 6–12, six grades), lower secondary (Gymnasium, ages 12–15, three grades, compulsory), and upper secondary (Lyceum, ages 15–18, three grades, non-compulsory). After primary school, students automatically progress to Gymnasium, with no entry exams required. Core subjects, including English, are compulsory from kindergarten through secondary education, and grading systems shift from descriptive assessments in early years to numerical scores in upper grades. Special schools and evening schools exist for varied educational needs, and there are multiple types of secondary schools such as model, music, art, vocational, and cross-cultural schools.
Upper secondary education offers both general and vocational pathways. Lyceum students can take Pan-Hellenic Examinations for university access, with admission based on a combination of exam results and academic performance. Vocational schools (EPAL, EPAS, SAEK) provide specialized training and dual diplomas, with options for apprenticeship and pathways into higher education. Tertiary education is delivered by public and private Higher Education Institutes (HEIs), primarily universities and academies; public HEIs are tuition-free for undergraduate studies and most students, though fees may apply in some postgraduate programs. Greece also features non-formal education options, extensive vocational training tracks, and lifelong learning centers. The Hellenic Qualification Framework (HQF) aligns formal and non-formal qualifications to European standards, ensuring comparability across educational levels.
